title: Public health and epidemiology
note: Epidemiology measures how often health events occur in populations and why. Incidence counts new cases over a period; prevalence counts all existing cases at a time. R0 tells how fast an infection can spread, and study designs (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional, randomized trial) differ in how they link exposures to outcomes.

read.title: R0 and herd immunity
text: The basic reproduction number, R0, is the average number of new infections caused by one infected person in a population where everyone is susceptible. It depends on the pathogen, how people contact each other, and how long someone stays infectious. If each case causes more than one new case, an outbreak grows; if fewer than one, it fades.

As people become immune, through infection or vaccination, each case meets fewer susceptible people. The effective reproduction number, often written Rt, then falls below R0. Spread stops being self-sustaining once Rt drops below 1. In the simplest model this happens when the immune share of the population exceeds 1 − 1/R0. For an infection with an R0 of 4, that threshold is about 75 percent; a more contagious infection needs a higher share.

This is herd immunity: protection that reaches people who are not themselves immune, such as newborns too young for a vaccine or people whose immune systems cannot respond to one. Real populations are not evenly mixed, so pockets with low immunity can still sustain outbreaks even when the overall average looks high enough.

q.q: What does an Rt below 1 mean?
o: Each case causes fewer than one new case, so spread fades
